label: D2 after a2 -> S2 (common), when the policy preference for a2 is only weak
explanation: Fires only at DELAY_2 steps where the agent chose a2 and reached S2 by the common transition. It never fires at D1 or GO, after a1, or after any rare transition. That base condition has recall 1.0 and mass recall 1.0 but precision 0.29 (dev). Within it, the feature fires when the model is not strongly committed to a2: the policy logit difference choice = logit(a1) - logit(a2) at that step is above about -3.5. Adding this condition brings dev precision to 0.79, recall 0.79, F1 0.79 and mass recall 0.96. Strongly a2-committed steps (choice < -4.4) are almost always silent. Behavioural correlates of the same uncertainty raise the firing rate: the previous trial unrewarded (rate 0.067 vs 0.023), a switch onto a2 (stay = 0), S2 not currently good (chose_good = 0), early in the episode (rate falls to about 0 by trials 90-99), and high value. Dev F1 for (prev_reward == 0 | stay == 0) within the base condition is only 0.58, so the policy-confidence condition captures the structure better. Everything in the predicate is observable at D2; choice is the policy output of the model itself. This is a property of the model, not a task variable, so the verdict is partial.
